---STATUS---
# pathland-render-qt — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 28, 2026

The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.

**Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
- **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
  **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
  the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
  and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
- **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
  QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
  delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
  needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative`).

## Implemented

- **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
  Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
  links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
  `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
  core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
- **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
  `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
  set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
  `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
- **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
  emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
  commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
  preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
  renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
  clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
  are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
  `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
- **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
  `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
  `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
  padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
  `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
  `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
  unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
  `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
  → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
  handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
  activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
  (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
  `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
  (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
  `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
  native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
  (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
  FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
  `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
  property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
  value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
  `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
  prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
  `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
  (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
  **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
  `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
  slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
- **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
  *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
  attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
  the create-time contentItem placeholder.
- **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
  (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
  `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
  ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
  `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
- **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
  is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
  its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
  Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
  spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
  `DELETE`.
- **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
  `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
  renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
- **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
  fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
  shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
  concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
  init.
- **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
  `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
  C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
- **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
  an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
  idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
- **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
  on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
  `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
  `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
  a bare program name to Qt.
- **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
  Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
  the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
  shared ring).

- **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
  `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
  page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
  `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
  depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
  chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
  `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
  pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
  is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
  has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
  QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
  container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
  visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Pointer `hover`/`leave` flags (`POINTER_MOVE` hovering/leaving) and
  `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` listener bits are not yet reported; BackSpace as native
  back (text-focus detection) is deferred.
- The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
  does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
  tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
- The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` either (the spec table is
  aspirational) — the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH, but the Rust demo
  can't exercise nav without a DSL feature; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
  vehicle (Phase D).
- `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
  intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
- `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on stacks/controls (Qt Quick Controls own their
  background delegate; mapping is a follow-up), `SHAPE` path approximation,
  `MENU` popup item list, `DATE_PICKER`/`COLOR_PICKER` native dialogs, and
  `PICKER` option styling not yet mapped.
- **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
  `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid

# pathland-render-qt — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 28, 2026

The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.

**Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
- **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
  **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
  the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
  and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
- **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
  QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
  delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
  needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative`).

## Implemented

- **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
  Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
  links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
  `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
  core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
- **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
  `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
  set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
  `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
- **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
  emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
  commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
  preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
  renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
  clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
  are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
  `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
- **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
  `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
  `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
  padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
  `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
  `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
  unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
  `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
  → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
  handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
  activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
  (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
  `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
  (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
  `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
  native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
  (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
  FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
  `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
  property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
  value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
  `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
  prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
  `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
  (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
  **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
  `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
  slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
- **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
  *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
  attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
  the create-time contentItem placeholder.
- **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
  (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
  `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
  ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
  `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
- **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
  is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
  its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
  Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
  spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
  `DELETE`.
- **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
  `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
  renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
- **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
  fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
  shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
  concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
  init.
- **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
  `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
  C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
- **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
  an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
  idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
- **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
  on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
  `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
  `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
  a bare program name to Qt.
- **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
  Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
  the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
  shared ring).

- **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
  `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
  page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
  `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
  depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
  chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
  `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
  pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
  is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
  has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
  QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
  container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
  visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Pointer `hover`/`leave` flags (`POINTER_MOVE` hovering/leaving) and
  `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` listener bits are not yet reported; BackSpace as native
  back (text-focus detection) is deferred.
- The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
  does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
  tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
- The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` either (the spec table is
  aspirational) — the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH, but the Rust demo
  can't exercise nav without a DSL feature; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
  vehicle (Phase D).
- `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
  intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
- `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on stacks/controls (Qt Quick Controls own their

- Lazy views render eagerly.

# Pathland Media Kit

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 17, 2026

---

## Introduction

Media playback in Pathland is split into two roles:

- a **media controller** ([`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`](./PRIMITIVES.md#media-controller--media_controller-0x30)
  `0x30`) — a **non-visual** node that owns a media resource and its transport
  state (source, play/pause, position, volume, …); and
- a **video surface** ([`VIDEO`](./PRIMITIVES.md#video--video-0x0a) `0x0A`) — the
  only media *view*: it references a controller and renders its video output.

**Audio has no view of its own.** Audio is non-visual: an audio playback is a
controller plus the application's **own** views (buttons, sliders, labels) bound
to the controller's transport signals. There are **no renderer-native audio
controls** — the application defines the entire control surface in code. The
former `AUDIO` component is therefore **removed**.

Before this document, playback identity *was* the media node id: the source and
the transport properties lived on the `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node itself, and the media
events reported against it. That makes a **structural swap** of the media node —
the normal case under `SIZE_THAT_FITS`, conditional rendering, or any subtree
replacement — destroy the playback, and it makes "control the same playback from
two places" inexpressible.

The controller/surface split fixes both: playback identity is the **controller**
node id, which the application keeps **outside** the swapping branch, so a swap
re-attaches a view to a playback that never stopped — and for audio the swapping
thing is just the application's own control views.

There is **one** controller component for both audio and video — the transport is
the same thing in both cases, exactly as SwiftUI has one `AVPlayer` for both and
`VideoPlayer` is merely a view over it. **Kind is decided by the views**: a
controller with a `VIDEO` surface renders video; a controller with no media view
is audio.

This document specifies the media contract: the controller node, the video
surface binding, transport commands vs. reports, the event family, and the swap
rules. It adds **one component**, **five properties**, and **one event**, and
removes the `AUDIO` component — no new opcode category, and no change to the wire
format.

### Relationship to the other specs

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format (16-byte opcode, categories, value types, `PLPL` batches) |
| [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | The `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` component and the `VIDEO` surface |
| [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | The media property ids and their value types |
| [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | The `MEDIA_*` event family, its guards, and the echo rules |
| [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md) | The controller's layout transparency and media content fitting |
| [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden vectors for the controller component and the binding property |
| **MEDIA.md** (this file) | The end-to-end media contract |

---

## 1. The model

```
MEDIA_CONTROLLER 0x30            non-visual; owns the resource + transport
  MEDIA_SOURCE
  PLAYBACK_STATE / MEDIA_POSITION / MEDIA_VOLUME
  MEDIA_MUTED / MEDIA_LOOP / MEDIA_RATE
        ▲                                        ▲
        │ MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID                    │ bound transport signals
        │                                        │
   VIDEO 0x0A                            application views
   (renders the video output)            (buttons/sliders/labels —
                                          the ENTIRE audio control surface)
```

- The **controller** is a node in the application's retained tree, but it is
  **layout-transparent** (§2.2): it occupies no space and renders no element.
- A **video surface** is an ordinary view node wherever the application wants it
  in the layout. It names a controller with `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (0x103A). It is
  **not** a child of the controller — the relationship is a **reference**, not a
  parent/child edge. The two nodes may live anywhere in the tree, and their
  relative position carries no meaning.
- **Audio has no view.** An audio playback is controlled by ordinary application
  views whose actions/values write the controller's transport properties. Nothing
  in the protocol renders audio.
- The application **SHOULD** place a controller at a stable position that no
  structural swap removes — e.g. a sibling of (or ancestor of) the `SIZE_THAT_FITS`
  slot, or a child of the root. A controller inside a swapping branch would be
  created and destroyed with that branch, defeating the split.

### 1.1 What lives where

| Concern | Owner |
|---------|-------|
| The media resource (source URL/asset) | controller — `MEDIA_SOURCE` |
| Transport state (play, seek, volume, mute, loop, rate) | controller |
| Transport **commands** from the app | controller (properties) |
| Transport **reports** to the app | controller (events target its id) |
| Whether a visual is shown, and its box/content mode | `VIDEO` surface |
| The video control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | `VIDEO` surface |
| The **audio** control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | the application's own views (no protocol surface) |
| Renderer-native vs. custom **video** controls | `VIDEO` dual mode (native when it has no children, the children when it has) |

---

## 2. The controller — `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30

### 2.1 Protocol

- A **leaf** node: it has no children. A `VIDEO` surface references it by id;
  it is not that surface's child.
- It carries the media resource and the transport properties (§2.3).
- It is created, updated, and deleted like any other node (`TREE` `CREATE_NODE` /
  `DELETE_NODE`), so it participates in the ordinary structural diff, in a
  full-snapshot (`META::RESYNC`), and in proxy-id remapping
  ([PROXY.md](./PROXY.md)) with no media-specific machinery.
- A controller is **not** a media surface and never renders a visual.

=========== PROXY ===========

# Pathland Media Kit

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 17, 2026

---

## Introduction

Media playback in Pathland is split into two roles:

- a **media controller** ([`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`](./PRIMITIVES.md#media-controller--media_controller-0x30)
  `0x30`) — a **non-visual** node that owns a media resource and its transport
  state (source, play/pause, position, volume, …); and
- a **video surface** ([`VIDEO`](./PRIMITIVES.md#video--video-0x0a) `0x0A`) — the
  only media *view*: it references a controller and renders its video output.

**Audio has no view of its own.** Audio is non-visual: an audio playback is a
controller plus the application's **own** views (buttons, sliders, labels) bound
to the controller's transport signals. There are **no renderer-native audio
controls** — the application defines the entire control surface in code. The
former `AUDIO` component is therefore **removed**.

Before this document, playback identity *was* the media node id: the source and
the transport properties lived on the `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node itself, and the media
events reported against it. That makes a **structural swap** of the media node —
the normal case under `SIZE_THAT_FITS`, conditional rendering, or any subtree
replacement — destroy the playback, and it makes "control the same playback from
two places" inexpressible.

The controller/surface split fixes both: playback identity is the **controller**
node id, which the application keeps **outside** the swapping branch, so a swap
re-attaches a view to a playback that never stopped — and for audio the swapping
thing is just the application's own control views.

There is **one** controller component for both audio and video — the transport is
the same thing in both cases, exactly as SwiftUI has one `AVPlayer` for both and
`VideoPlayer` is merely a view over it. **Kind is decided by the views**: a
controller with a `VIDEO` surface renders video; a controller with no media view
is audio.

This document specifies the media contract: the controller node, the video
surface binding, transport commands vs. reports, the event family, and the swap
rules. It adds **one component**, **five properties**, and **one event**, and
removes the `AUDIO` component — no new opcode category, and no change to the wire
format.

### Relationship to the other specs

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format (16-byte opcode, categories, value types, `PLPL` batches) |
| [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | The `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` component and the `VIDEO` surface |
| [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | The media property ids and their value types |
| [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | The `MEDIA_*` event family, its guards, and the echo rules |
| [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md) | The controller's layout transparency and media content fitting |
| [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden vectors for the controller component and the binding property |
| **MEDIA.md** (this file) | The end-to-end media contract |

---

## 1. The model

```
MEDIA_CONTROLLER 0x30            non-visual; owns the resource + transport
  MEDIA_SOURCE
  PLAYBACK_STATE / MEDIA_POSITION / MEDIA_VOLUME
  MEDIA_MUTED / MEDIA_LOOP / MEDIA_RATE
        ▲                                        ▲
        │ MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID                    │ bound transport signals
        │                                        │
   VIDEO 0x0A                            application views
   (renders the video output)            (buttons/sliders/labels —
                                          the ENTIRE audio control surface)
```

- The **controller** is a node in the application's retained tree, but it is
  **layout-transparent** (§2.2): it occupies no space and renders no element.
- A **video surface** is an ordinary view node wherever the application wants it
  in the layout. It names a controller with `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (0x103A). It is
  **not** a child of the controller — the relationship is a **reference**, not a
  parent/child edge. The two nodes may live anywhere in the tree, and their
  relative position carries no meaning.
- **Audio has no view.** An audio playback is controlled by ordinary application
  views whose actions/values write the controller's transport properties. Nothing
  in the protocol renders audio.
- The application **SHOULD** place a controller at a stable position that no
  structural swap removes — e.g. a sibling of (or ancestor of) the `SIZE_THAT_FITS`
  slot, or a child of the root. A controller inside a swapping branch would be
  created and destroyed with that branch, defeating the split.

### 1.1 What lives where

| Concern | Owner |
|---------|-------|
| The media resource (source URL/asset) | controller — `MEDIA_SOURCE` |
| Transport state (play, seek, volume, mute, loop, rate) | controller |
| Transport **commands** from the app | controller (properties) |
| Transport **reports** to the app | controller (events target its id) |
| Whether a visual is shown, and its box/content mode | `VIDEO` surface |
| The video control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | `VIDEO` surface |
| The **audio** control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | the application's own views (no protocol surface) |
| Renderer-native vs. custom **video** controls | `VIDEO` dual mode (native when it has no children, the children when it has) |

---

## 2. The controller — `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30

### 2.1 Protocol

- A **leaf** node: it has no children. A `VIDEO` surface references it by id;
  it is not that surface's child.
- It carries the media resource and the transport properties (§2.3).
- It is created, updated, and deleted like any other node (`TREE` `CREATE_NODE` /
  `DELETE_NODE`), so it participates in the ordinary structural diff, in a
  full-snapshot (`META::RESYNC`), and in proxy-id remapping
  ([PROXY.md](./PROXY.md)) with no media-specific machinery.
- A controller is **not** a media surface and never renders a visual.

# Icons — the `ICON` primitive and canonical vocabulary

The `ICON` primitive (0x0B) renders a **renderer-native symbol** for a canonical,
semantic name written once in the UI model. Unlike `IMAGE` (an asset loaded from
a URL), an icon is a *word* the renderer maps onto its platform's native icon
set.

> **The spec is the vocabulary contract only.** It lists the icons that are
> spec'ed — the `ICON_NAME` values every renderer MUST understand. **Which
> native glyph each renderer draws for a name is renderer-owned** (like the
> concrete values of design tokens): the mapping never appears in the spec;
> each renderer defines its own.

The **application owns the intent** (the neutral name); the **renderer owns the
visual** (which glyph, its default size, its weighting). This mirrors the design
tokens' split (spec/TOKENS.md).

## Protocol

- **Component**: `ICON` `0x0B` (leaf).
- **Property**: `ICON_NAME` `0x1038` (`STRING`, arena ref) — the canonical name.
- Reuses: `LABEL` (accessibility — a `LABEL` makes the icon presentable, absent
  makes it decorative), `COLOR` / `foregroundStyle` (tint), `FONT_SIZE` (size —
  text-style symbol sizing; the renderer owns its default size when absent), and
  the frame/opacity modifiers.
- `ICON` is a leaf like `IMAGE` — no new events, no children.

## Canonical vocabulary

`ICON_NAME` values are the *protocol contract*. The canonical names live in
`pathland_core::constants::icon` (`NAMES`, `is_canonical`) — the single
protocol-authoritative list every renderer and DSL binds to. An app may
reference a name the vocabulary does not (yet) contain; renderers fall back
however they own the mapping does, and the vocabulary can grow.

- **Navigation**: `home` `search` `menu` `close` `chevron-left` `chevron-right`
  `chevron-up` `chevron-down` `arrow-left` `arrow-right`
- **Actions**: `add` `remove` `check` `edit` `delete` `save` `share` `download`
  `upload` `refresh` `lock` `logout`
- **Media**: `play` `pause` `stop` `skip-back` `skip-forward` `volume`
  `volume-mute` `shuffle` `repeat` `music`
- **Status**: `info` `warning` `error` `success` `heart` `star` `bell` `cloud`
- **People**: `user` `users`
- **System**: `settings` `grid` `list` `filter`
- **Content**: `folder` `file` `image`

## Semantics

- **Authoring**: `Icon.make(i -> i.name(IconName.PLAY))` /
  `Icon.make(i -> i.name("play"))` (a canonical string, or an app-extension
  name), `Label.make(l -> l.title(title).icon(icon))`,
  `Button.make(b -> b.action(action)).children(Icon.make(i -> i.name(…)))`.
- **Size / tint**: `FONT_SIZE` / `COLOR` as on text. Sized like a symbol (the
  renderer owns its default size); tinted for the active scheme.
- **Reactivity**: the name is a single `Signal<String>` — a change re-emits only
  the node's `ICON_NAME` delta.
- **Accessibility**: `LABEL` makes the icon presentable; without one the icon is
  decorative (not announced, not interactive).

## Adding an icon

The user is asking a good architectural question: the current Qt integration is built in Rust (with a thin C++ layer via cc/moc), and they're wondering whether it would be better to rewrite the renderer from scratch in C++ since C++ is Qt Quick's primary/supported language.

This is a "weighing tradeoffs" question. I should give a well-reasoned recommendation. Let me understand the current architecture better to give an informed answer.

Key facts I already know:
- The Qt renderer is hybrid: Rust owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), delta diff, Pump transport seam, Qt main-loop shell, C ABI. C++ (in src/qt/) owns the Qt app shell + applies delta command batch to QML items. Built via cc + moc in build.rs.
- The whole architecture principle is: `pathland-render-core` is a "shared, toolkit-free" decode path that EVERY renderer shares (GTK, Qt, HTML). This is a deliberate design decision in AGENTS.md.

So the question is really: does it make sense to rewrite the Qt renderer in pure C++?

Let me think about the tradeoffs honestly.

Arguments FOR pure C++ rewrite:
1. Qt Quick / QML is natively C++/QML. Qt's own APIs (QML types, QQmlEngine, QQmlComponent) are C++. Writing in C++ avoids the Rust<->C++ FFI boundary and the build.rs moc/cc complexity.
2. The current FFI boundary (flat command batch, PathlandQtCommand/PathlandQtEvent structs) is a hand-maintained marshalling layer that duplicates work and adds friction.
3. Moc/cc build complexity in build.rs (locating qmake, moc, frameworks) is fragile.
4. Qt Quick Controls are QML; mixing Rust for logic + C++/QML for UI is awkward. A pure C++/QML renderer could use QML directly.

Arguments AGAINST pure C++ rewrite (i.e., keep hybrid Rust+C++ or move more to Rust):
1. The whole protocol/core is Rust. `pathland-core` (the opcode decode, ring, arena, events, design tokens) is Rust and `no_std`/wasm. Rewriting in C++ would require reimplementing the 16-byte opcode decoder, ring buffer, arena, design token resolution, event encoding in C++ — duplicating a large, tested surface.
2. The shared `pathland-render-core` is "toolkit-free" and shared across GTK/Qt/HTML. This is a NON-NEGOTIABLE architectural principle: "every renderer shares one tested decode path." Moving Qt to pure C++ breaks that shared decode — you'd have two decode implementations (Rust for GTK/HTML, C++ for Qt) that can drift.
3. The protocol conformance is enforced by golden vectors in Rust tests. A C++ decode would need its own conformance tests.
4. The event ring / shared-memory ring / C ABI (`pathland_qt_run_ring`, `NativeHost`) is Rust, consumed by Java JNA, Swift, etc. The renderer needs to interop with that ring via the C ABI regardless.
5. The delta diff + reactive emission "zero opcodes for unchanged tree" logic is Rust and tested. Reimplementing in C++ risks bugs.

Actually, let me think about what "better" means here. The question is fundamentally about whether the hybrid approach is sound, or whether a rewrite would reduce friction.

The hybrid design (Rust core + thin C++/QML layer) is actually a reasonable and common pattern. The alternative "pure C++ renderer" would still need to talk to the Rust protocol core (for the ring, events, decode) via some boundary — UNLESS they also rewrite the protocol decode in C++.

Wait — but actually, there's a nuance. The renderers are "dumb" consumers of the opcode stream. The opcode stream is emitted by the application (Rust DSL or Java DSL). The renderer decodes it. The decode is currently in Rust (pathland-render-core). 

If they rewrite the Qt renderer in C++, they'd reimplement:
- The opcode frame decode (16-byte opcode → RenderTree/HostNode).
- Design token resolution.
- Delta diff (sent-state cache).
- Event encoding.
- Ring transport interop (still needs to read the shared ring written by the Rust/Java app via libpathland_core).

That's a LOT of duplicated logic. The whole point of `pathland-render-core` is to NOT do that per-renderer.

But there's a middle path: keep the Rust decode core (as a cdylib exposing a C ABI), and have a pure C++/QML renderer consume it via the C ABI. Actually that's basically what already happens — the Java `pathland-render-html` does exactly this (JNA shim over the Rust HTML renderer). And the Qt renderer already exposes `pathland_qt_run` C ABI.

So the real question is: where to draw the line? Currently the line is:
- Rust: decode (render-core) + delta diff + command batch emission + shell + C ABI.
- C++: QML scene graph application of the command batch.

A pure C++ rewrite would move decode+diff into C++ too, or keep decode in Rust and only move the "apply" part to C++ (which is already the case).

Let me be honest and balanced. I'll present:
1. What the current architecture actually is (correcting any misreading — the current one is already mostly C++ for the Qt-specific part).
2. The tradeoffs.
3. A recommendation.

My recommendation: Do NOT rewrite from scratch in C++. The current hybrid is sound because:
- The decode/diff/token-resolution is the hard, shared, tested part — keep it in Rust (`pathland-render-core`) for the non-negotiable "one tested decode path" principle.
- The Qt-specific "apply to QML" is already C++/QML, which is exactly right.
- The friction (FFI command batch) is real but bounded; a rewrite re-creates the bigger, riskier decode surface in C++.

But I should acknowledge there are legitimate pain points and offer an option: if the FFI boundary is painful, one could move MORE of the renderer into C++ (e.g., do the delta-diff/command-batch generation in C++ while keeping decode in Rust), but that's a refactor, not a rewrite.

This significantly informs my answer. The branch's whole thesis is "extract a shared, toolkit-free decode core used by GTK and Qt." The merge must reconcile main's newer GTK (with media/proxy/icons/fit) against the branch's extracted render-core — meaning render-core must absorb all of main's GTK decode advancements too.

So for the user's question: rewriting Qt in C++ would go against the branch's own architectural direction (shared Rust decode core). The branch just did the opposite — it extracted the decode into Rust so GTK and Qt share it. Rewriting Qt's decode in C++ would create a THIRD decode implementation.

Now I can give a well-grounded answer. Let me summarize my recommendation clearly.

The honest, balanced answer:

1. Clarify: the Qt renderer is already hybrid — the Qt/QML-specific part (widget mapping, the thing "is Qt") is already C++ (qt_layer.cpp ~1556 lines + bridge.cpp). Rust owns only the protocol decode/diff/token/ABI — the non-Qt-specific part.

2. The real question: where should the *protocol decode + diff + token resolution* live? The branch just deliberately extracted this into shared Rust (`pathland-render-core`) so GTK and Qt (and future renderers) share ONE tested decode. Rewriting the Qt renderer "from scratch in C++" would either:
   (a) reimplement decode+diff+tokens in C++ → duplicates the single most correctness-critical, conformance-tested code, and breaks the "one tested decode path" principle; or
   (b) keep decode in Rust and only write the Qt shell in C++ → which is exactly what exists today.

3. So "pure C++ from scratch" isn't really better; it's a step backward for correctness/consistency, with the only gain being removal of the Rust↔C++ FFI marshalling layer.

4. Where the FFI friction is real, the fix is to shrink/adjust the boundary (e.g., move the delta-diff into C++ while keeping decode in Rust, or make the command batch a thinner passthrough), not to rewrite.

5. The one legitimate C++-native argument: QML is declarative, and the current C++ layer uses imperative `QObject::setProperty`/`QQuickItem` construction. A more idiomatic C++/QML renderer could generate QML declarations or use `QQmlComponent`-driven factories. But that's an improvement *within* the C++ layer, orthogonal to Rust-vs-C++.

Recommendation: Keep the hybrid architecture (Rust shared decode + C++/QML widget layer). Don't rewrite from scratch. If the goal is to reduce the FFI seam, refactor where the boundary sits, but don't reimplement the protocol in C++.

I should also mention the merge implication: the branch already moved GTK onto the shared core, and main advanced GTK's decode substantially (media/proxy/icons/fit). So either way, render-core must absorb main's GTK decode work — that's the real cost, independent of Qt language choice.

Let me also give the "what would a pure C++ rewrite actually cost" concrete list:
- Reimplement 16-byte opcode frame decode (TREE/PARAMETER/EVENT/META), arena strings, value-type packing.
- Reimplement design-token resolution + color-scheme detection.
- Reimplement sent-state delta diff (zero-opcode property).
- Reimplement event encoding (all the MEDIA_*, pointer, key, value, text events) + echo suppression.

## Short answer: no — keep the hybrid, don't rewrite in C++

First, a correction to the premise: the Qt integration is **already hybrid, and the part that is actually Qt is already C++**. The split is roughly even:

| Layer | Language | File(s) |
|-------|----------|---------|
| Qt/QML widget mapping, QML `Bridge` QObject | **C++** | `qt_layer.cpp` (1556 ln), `bridge.cpp` (84 ln) |
| Protocol decode, sent-state delta diff, token resolution, ring/C ABI | Rust | `render-core/host.rs`, `renderer.rs`, `ffi.rs`, `run.rs`, `capi.rs` |

So "Qt Quick's native language" is already where it needs to be — the actual scene-graph/widget work is C++. What's in Rust is **not Qt-specific at all**: it's the 16-byte opcode decode, design-token resolution, and diff logic.

### What a "pure C++ from scratch" rewrite actually means

You'd only be moving the **protocol layer** into C++, and you'd reimplement in C++:

- 16-byte opcode frame decode (TREE/PARAMETER/EVENT/META, arena strings, value-type packing)
- design-token resolution + color-scheme detection
- the sent-state delta diff ("unchanged tree emits zero opcodes")
- the entire event encoder (pointer/key/value/text + the new `MEDIA_*` family, echo suppression)
- ring/transport interop against `libpathland_core`
- golden-vector conformance tests

…and then maintain **two** decoders forever: Rust (GTK + HTML) and C++ (Qt), so every protocol change lands twice. That's the exact thing this branch just spent effort *eliminating*.

### The key fact you should know about this branch's direction

`pathland-render-core` (the shared Rust decode) **does not exist on `main`** — it was introduced on `feat/qt-renderer`, and the branch **also refactored GTK onto it** (`pathland-render-gtk/Cargo.toml` → `pathland-render-core`). So the whole thesis of this branch is "one tested, toolkit-free decode shared by every renderer." A C++ rewrite of Qt's decode directly contradicts that.

Note also: `main` advanced GTK's decode substantially (media/proxy/icons/fit). **Regardless of Qt's language choice**, `render-core` must absorb that work during the merge. That's the real cost, and it's independent of the Rust-vs-C++ question.

### What the actual pain point is (and it's not the language)

The real friction is the **Rust↔C++ FFI marshalling layer** (`PathlandQtCommand` batch + `PathlandQtEvent` in `ffi.rs`), not the language. If that seam bugs you, the fix is to *move where the boundary sits* — e.g. keep the decode in Rust and push the delta-diff down into C++ — rather than reimplement the protocol.

The one legitimate "more idiomatic C++" critique is that `qt_layer.cpp` builds QML items imperatively via `QObject::setProperty`, where QML prefers declarative construction (`QQmlComponent`-driven factories or generated QML). That's an improvement **inside the C++ layer**, orthogonal to Rust-vs-C++.

---

**Recommendation:** stay with the agreed hybrid plan (Rust shared decode + C++/QML widget layer). It keeps one conformance-tested decode, keeps ring/ABI interop in Rust where it already is, and the C++ layer already owns everything Qt-specific.

**Phase 0 — Merge & re-platform**
1. `git merge main`, resolve `pathland-core` conflicts (`constants.rs`, `conformance.rs`, `events.rs`, `lib.rs`, `ring.rs`, tests).
2. Absorb main's GTK decode advancements into `pathland-render-core` (media/proxy/icons/fit), since the branch already moved GTK onto it.

4. Extend shared decode for `SET_DATE` (0x04) + new component/event/property ids.
5. **Gate:** `cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-render-core`, `cargo build -p pathland-render-qt` (offscreen), wasm no_std guard.

+# publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
+# to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
+# platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
+#
+# The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
+# workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
+# a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
+# is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
+# suffix is allowed).
+#
+# The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
+# safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
+# re-deploy of an existing version).
+#
+# Secrets:
+#   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
+#   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
+#   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
+#   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
+#   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password
+
+on:
+  release:
+    types: [published]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      tag:
+        description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
+        required: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+jobs:
+  version:
+    name: Resolve + validate version
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
+      version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
+    steps:
+      - id: v
+        name: Derive the version from the tag
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
+          if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
+            echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          version="${tag#v}"
+          echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
+          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

+    name: Publish crates to crates.io
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: version
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
+      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

+        working-directory: lib/rust
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
+          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"

+          awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
+          grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u
+
+      - name: Test the publishable crates
+        working-directory: lib/rust
+        run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html
+
+      - name: Publish in dependency order
+        working-directory: lib/rust
+        env:
+          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
+          crates=(pathland-core pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
+          for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
+            echo "::group::publish $c $version"
+            # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
+            if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
+              echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
+              echo "::endgroup::"
+              continue
+            fi
+            # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
+            # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
+            # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
+            cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
+            echo "::endgroup::"
+            # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
+            sleep 20
+          done
+
+      - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
+        working-directory: lib/rust
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
+          for c in pathland-core pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
+            cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
+          done

+      - name: Upload the .crate files
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: crates
+          path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  java-natives:
+    name: Build renderer natives (${{ matrix.platform }})
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
+    needs: version
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        include:
+          - { platform: windows-x86_64, runner: windows-latest }
+          - { platform: linux-x86_64, runner: ubuntu-latest }
+          - { platform: linux-aarch64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm }
+          - { platform: macos-aarch64, runner: macos-14 }
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
+      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
+
+      - name: Build the renderer cdylib
+        working-directory: lib/rust
+        run: cargo build --release -p pathland-render-html
+
+      - name: Stage the platform lib
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          case "${{ matrix.platform }}" in
+            windows-*) src="pathland_render_html.dll";      dst="libpathland_render_html.dll" ;;
+            macos-*)   src="libpathland_render_html.dylib"; dst="libpathland_render_html.dylib" ;;
+            *)         src="libpathland_render_html.so";    dst="libpathland_render_html.so" ;;
+          esac
+          dest="lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}"
+          mkdir -p "$dest"
+          cp "lib/rust/target/release/$src" "$dest/$dst"
+          ls -la "$dest"
+
+      - name: Upload the platform lib
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: native-${{ matrix.platform }}
+          path: lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}/*
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  java:
+    name: Publish to Maven Central
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: [version, java-natives]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
+
+      - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
+        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
+        with:
+          distribution: temurin
+          java-version: '17'
+          cache: maven
+          server-id: central
+          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
+          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
+          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
+          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

+      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
+      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
+      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
+      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          v=3.9.9
+          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"

+          mvn -v
+
+      - name: Set the version from the tag
+        working-directory: lib/java
+        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
+
+      - name: Download the platform natives
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          path: natives
+
+      - name: Stage the natives for the jar embed
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native
+          for d in natives/native-*; do
+            platform="${d#natives/native-}"
+            mkdir -p "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform"
+            cp "$d"/* "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform/"
+          done
+          find lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native -type f
+
+      # The demos are excluded from the release reactor: central-publishing-maven-plugin
+      # bundles every reactor module (it ignores maven.deploy.skip), and the demos must
+      # not be published.
+      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
+        working-directory: lib/java
+        env:
+          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
+          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
+          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
+        run: >-
+          mvn -B -P release deploy
+          -pl '!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'
+
+      - name: Collect the published main jars
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p dist/jars
+          for m in pathland-view pathland-view-processor pathland-render-html pathland-state-redis \
+                   pathland-server-core pathland-observability pathland-test-kit \
+                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus-starter; do
+            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
+          done
+          rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
+          ls -la dist/jars
+
+      - name: Upload the main jars
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: jars
+          path: dist/jars/*.jar
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  bump:
+    name: Commit the version back to main
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: [version, rust, java]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: main
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
+      - name: Set the Rust version
+        working-directory: lib/rust
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
+          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
+        with:
+          distribution: temurin
+          java-version: '17'
+      - name: Set the Java version
+        working-directory: lib/java
+        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
+
+      - name: Commit + push
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

+            echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          git add -A
+          git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
+          git push origin HEAD:main
+
+  release-assets:
+    name: Attach release assets
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: [version, rust, java-natives, java]
+    steps:
+      - name: Download all build artifacts
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          path: dist
+
+      - name: Collect the files to attach
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p out
+          find dist -type f \( -name '*.crate' -o -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.dll' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' \) -exec cp {} out/ \;
+          ls -la out
+
+      - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: gh release upload "${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}" out/* --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --clobber

 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.

 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Java with the hand-written
 > **`com.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
 > through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared
 > ring on desktop.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.

 ### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native` + `pathland-core-capi`)
 
 The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
 flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
 functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java/C# via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Java DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
 raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
 `ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Java DSL
 (`com.pathland.view.ffm`) binds it with **JNA** (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and
 owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.
 
 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
-- Java demo loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and calls
-  `pathland_gtk_run(host, on_event)`; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT`
-  opcodes through the shared ring. The renderer **writes** the events and
-  **wakes** the host (no payload); the host drains the event ring itself via
-  `pathland_native_drain_events` (Rust: `NativeHost::drain_events` /
-  `RingTransport::drain_events`). Events are never delivered through a
-  side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
+- Java demo (`pathland-gtk-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and
+  calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Java DSL's own
+  `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
+  ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
+  drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
+  delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
+  The demo mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared views the web demos use) with the
+  app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
+  `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
+  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
+  (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.

-| STYLE | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
+| PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment |

 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark), token resolution, effective color-scheme detection (platform-derived), interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`)
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 
 Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system) and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).

 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/`pathland-render-gtk` + tests
 4. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or

 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |

+# Releasing Pathland
+
+Publishing a **GitHub Release** (tagged `vX.Y.Z`) runs
+`.github/workflows/release.yml`, which sets the version from the tag, builds and
+publishes every artifact, attaches the built files to the Release, and commits
+the version back to `main`:
+
+| Ecosystem | Artifacts | Registry |
+|-----------|-----------|----------|
+| Rust | `pathland-core`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-render-html` | crates.io |
+| Java | `dev.pathland:*` libraries (incl. the renderer's native libs for windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64) | Maven Central |
+
+## Versioning (tag-driven)
+
+**The tag drives the version** — no pre-bump commit is needed:
+
+- The workflow writes `X.Y.Z` (from the tag `vX.Y.Z`) into
+  `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version` + the intra-workspace
+  path-dep pins, via `cargo set-version --workspace`) and
+  `lib/java/pom.xml` (via `mvn versions:set`) **in CI**, then publishes.
+- A `bump` job then commits that version back to `main`, so `main` always
+  reflects the latest release.
+
+Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release suffix is
+allowed); the `version` job fails on anything else. Releases are immutable per
+version — pick a new tag to re-release.
+
+## One-time setup
+
+Repository secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions):
+
+- `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` — a crates.io API token with publish scope
+  (https://crates.io/settings/tokens).
+- `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` — an armored GPG private key whose public key is on a
+  keyserver (Central verifies the signatures).
+- `GPG_PASSPHRASE` — that key's passphrase.
+- `CENTRAL_USERNAME` / `CENTRAL_PASSWORD` — a Sonatype Central Portal **user
+  token** (https://central.sonatype.com/account).
+
+Also: `main` must be pushable by the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the `bump` job).
+If `main` is protected, allow the Actions bot, or the bump step fails (after a
+successful publish).
+
+## Release
+
+1. Create a **GitHub Release** on `main` tagged `vX.Y.Z` (publish it).
+2. The workflow runs:
+   - `version` — derive + validate `X.Y.Z` from the tag.
+   - `rust` — set the version, test the publishable crates, publish them to
+     crates.io in dependency order, upload the `.crate` files.
+   - `java-natives` — build `libpathland_render_html` for windows-x86_64,
+     linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64.
+    - `java` — set the version, stage the natives into the renderer jar, run
+      `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central (auto-published after validation).
+    - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
+    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
+      four native libs to the GitHub Release.
+
+The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
+writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
+which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos
+are **excluded from the release reactor** (`-pl '!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`)
+— `central-publishing-maven-plugin` bundles every reactor module, ignoring
+`maven.deploy.skip`, and the demos must not be published.
+
+The publish steps are **idempotent**: a crate+version already on crates.io is
+skipped, so re-running a partially failed release is safe (re-run the workflow
+via `workflow_dispatch`, passing the `tag`). Maven Central rejects a re-deploy of
+an existing version, so a Java re-run only helps if the Java deploy did not
+complete.
+
+## Local pre-flight
+
+Rust — `cargo publish --dry-run -p pathland-core` validates the leaf crate (the
+dependent crates can only be dry-run once their dependencies are on crates.io,
+so the ordered CI publish validates them).
+
+Java — `mvn -P release verify` builds and signs the sources/javadoc jars without
+uploading. It needs GPG installed and a `central` server in `~/.m2/settings.xml`:
+
+```xml
+<server>
+  <id>central</id>
+  <username>TOKEN_USERNAME</username>
+  <password>TOKEN_PASSWORD</password>
+</server>
+```
+
+## Publishable crates (dependency order)
+
+```
+pathland-core → pathland-engine → pathland-view → pathland-core-transport → pathland-render-html
+```
+
+(`pathland-view-native`, `pathland-core-capi`, `pathland-render-gtk`,
+`pathland-render-gtk-demo`, `pathland-html-golden`, `pathland-ts-codegen` are
+**not** published — C-ABI cdylibs, the GTK renderer, and dev tools.)
+
+## Published Java modules
+
+`pathland-view`, `pathland-view-processor`, `pathland-render-html`,
+`pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-observability`,
+`pathland-test-kit`, `pathland-spring-boot-starter`, `pathland-quarkus-starter`
+(plus the `pathland-parent` POM). The demo modules
+(`pathland-demo-views`, `pathland-gtk-demo`, `pathland-quarkus-demo`,
+`pathland-spring-boot-demo`) set `maven.deploy.skip`.

+public final class HomeView implements View {

 # pathland-gtk-demo (Java) — implementation status
 
-**Last updated:** September 14, 2026
+**Last updated:** September 29, 2026
 
-Runs the shared framework-agnostic demo views (`com.pathland.demo`, e.g.
-`SplitNavDemo`) under the **native GTK4 renderer** (`libpathland_gtk`) — the
+Runs the shared framework-agnostic demo views (`dev.pathland.demo`, e.g.
+`MusicPlayerView`) under the **native GTK4 renderer** (`libpathland_gtk`) — the
 cross-language, shared-renderer story for Java. Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## How it works
 
 - The Java DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
   `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
 - The in-process GTK renderer pumps the same ring in place
   (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`, via `PathlandCore.ringMut`); no
   `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
 - Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains
   (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
-  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, router back).
+  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
+  router back).
 - State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
-  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme, and
-  `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` injected as a host signal (`/home`) — `SplitNavDemo`
-  reads it and builds its bound router.
+  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
+- **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks through a direct
+  GStreamer `playbin` (driven by the node's media control properties) and
+  reports `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
+  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths are resolved against a local asset root: the
+  demo extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-views` jar at
+  startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - `GtkRendererNative` — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
-  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)`); library resolved
-  from the `pathland.gtk.lib` system property or `java.library.path`.
+  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` +
+  `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root(dir)`); library resolved from the
+  `pathland.gtk.lib` system property or `java.library.path`.
 - `RingEventReader` — decodes raw ring `EVENT` opcodes into
-  `com.pathland.view.transport.Event`, resolving `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE`
-  strings from the shared host → guest event arena (header `0x40`).
-  Headless unit tests cover pointer/value/date/text/navigate decoding and
-  bounds behaviour.
-- `GtkHost` (`main`) — mounts `SplitNavDemo`, runs GTK (1100×720), drains and
-  dispatches events. Blocks until the window closes.
+  `dev.pathland.view.transport.Event`, resolving `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE`
+  strings from the shared host → guest event arena (header `0x40`), plus the
+  four `MEDIA_*` events (play state, time, ended, volume). Headless unit tests
+  cover pointer/value/date/text/navigate/media decoding and bounds behaviour.
+- `GtkHost` (`main`) — mounts `MusicPlayerView` (the Apple Music-style player:
+  library, now-playing sidebar, player bar with transport/seek/volume), extracts
+  the demo's audio + covers to a runtime dir, sets the asset root, runs GTK
+  (1180×800), drains and dispatches events. Blocks until the window closes.
 - The `Emitter` sets `BINDING_ID` on bound controls for `RingOpcodeSink`s (the
   GTK renderer gates `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED` on it).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
+- **Playback requires GStreamer** with the mp3 decoding plugins installed (the
+  brew `gstreamer` formula bundles them); without it the app runs but the
+  pipeline errors on play.
 - The GTK renderer's `attach_control_events` covers `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/
   `TEXT_FIELD`/`PICKER` only: `DATE_PICKER`, `STEPPER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, and
-  `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK — those sections
-  of the demo views are non-interactive on this path.
+  `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK.
 - macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` (GTK owns the main thread).
 - No automated GUI test (headless renderer tests live in `pathland-render-gtk`).
 
 ## Verified by
 
-`mvn test -pl pathland-gtk-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (5 tests, headless, no
-GTK). The full Java reactor compiles with this module.

+# pathland-observability — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** October 3, 2026
+
+Observability adapters for the framework-agnostic `pathland-server-core`
+telemetry seam. The core emits lifecycle/throughput events through
+`PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`); this module turns them into metrics and
+spans. Protocol/contract context: `spec/OPCODE.md`; the seam itself is in
+`pathland-server-core`.
+
+## Implemented
+
+- **`MicrometerTelemetry`** — a `PathlandTelemetry` over any Micrometer
+  `MeterRegistry` (Prometheus, OTLP, …). Metric catalog:
+  - `pathland.sessions.active` — gauge (pull-based, bound by the host)
+  - `pathland.sessions.opened` / `pathland.sessions.closed` — counters
+  - `pathland.events.received` — counter (decoded inbound events)
+  - `pathland.batches.sent` / `pathland.frames.sent` / `pathland.bytes.sent` — counters
+  - `pathland.batch.size` — distribution summary (opcodes per batch)
+  - `pathland.batch.flush` — timer (merge + encode)
+  - `pathland.ssr.render` — timer (SSR render round-trip)
+  - `pathland.resync.requested` — counter
+  - `pathland.ws.failures` — counter
+  - Every meter is tagged by `mount` (bounded). Registrations are idempotent, so
+    a builder per event is cheap and cannot leak meters.
+- **`TracingTelemetry`** — an OpenTelemetry decorator over another
+  `PathlandTelemetry`: emits a span per frame send (`pathland.frame.send`), per
+  inbound event batch (`pathland.event.batch`), and per SSR render
+  (`pathland.ssr.render`), with the wrapped telemetry still receiving every
+  event. Spans are back-dated by the measured duration so they render with the
+  real latency. Opt-in — the starters build it only when a `Tracer`/`OpenTelemetry`
+  bean is available.
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- No client-side (browser) telemetry — server-side only.
+- `ws.failures` does not tag the failure reason (unbounded cardinality).
+
+## Verified by
+
+`mvn test -pl pathland-observability` — `MicrometerTelemetryTest` (the full
+metric catalog + per-mount tagging) and `TracingTelemetryTest` (span names via an
+in-memory OTel exporter, plus delegation). The starters' tests assert the wiring
+end to end (`/q/health` + `/q/metrics`, `/actuator/health` + `pathland.*` meters).
